name: engineering
description: System design training — architecture, trade-offs, and constraint satisfaction.

modules.content: Start with constraints, not features. What must be true? Latency < X, throughput > Y, cost < Z. Architecture follows constraints. Every component exists because a constraint demands it.

You can't optimize everything simultaneously. Faster → more compute → more cost. More reliable → more redundancy → more complexity. The conservation law applies: γ+H = C − α·ln(V). Every gain in one dimension costs another.
Measure first. Current utilization, growth rate, peak multiplier. Plan for 2× current peak. Monitor conservation: when γ+H drifts, it's time to scale or shed load.

Constraints propagate. A constraint on latency propagates to compute, which propagates to cost. The constraint graph is the architecture. Find the tightest constraint — that's your bottleneck. Everything else is negotiable.
